pull.title: BIP-379: add test vectors from rust-miniscript
pull.body:
The BIP-379 currently has a `TBD` in the test vector section.
I have extracted a bunch of test vectors from the [`rust-miniscript`](https://github.com/rust-bitcoin/rust-miniscript/) project, either directly or by slightly modifying test code to dump them into text/TSV files.
They have been very helpful for re-implementation in another language, so I think they should be made easily available here.

events.body: Concept ACK. It may be handy to provide a file here that runs/verifies the test vectors.

> Concept ACK. It may be handy to provide a file here that runs/verifies the test vectors.

That's a great idea. I've added that in the latest push.
Output looks like this:

```shell
$ cd bip-0379; go run main.go
Checking the BIP379 test vectors in . against
github.com/btcsuite/btcd/descriptors/miniscript.

Testing vectors in valid_from_alloy.txt       [positive]: 5896/5896 done (type column not compared)
Testing vectors in valid_8f1e8_from_alloy.txt [positive]: 3492/3492 done (type column not compared)
Testing vectors in malleable_from_alloy.txt   [positive/negative]: 7024/7024 + 7024/7024 done
Testing vectors in conflict_from_alloy.txt    [positive]: 1773/1773 done (1586 of them are rejected by the sanity checks)
Testing vectors in edge_cases.txt             [positive]: 42/42 done
Testing vectors in opcodes.txt                [positive]: 18185/18185 done (type and op count columns not compared)
Testing vectors in invalid.txt                [negative]: 5574/5574 done
Testing vectors in props_from_rust.tsv        [positive]: 8198/8198 done (op_count and exec_stack columns not compared)
Testing vectors in props_from_rust_tap.tsv    [positive/negative]: 6728/6728 + 1470/1470 done (op_count and exec_stack columns not compared)
Testing vectors in scripts_from_rust.tsv      [positive]: 8198/8198 done
Testing vectors in scripts_from_rust_tap.tsv  [positive/negative]: 6728/6728 + 1470/1470 done
Testing vectors in redeem.json                [positive/negative]: 12/12 + 34/34 done (each spend is executed in the script engine)

All 81848 vectors passed (0 skipped).


```

I tried to run these tests through the Bitcoin Core miniscript implementation, but quickly hit the problem that the typing rules are inplemented inconsistently. This isn't a problem in production, because the differences are all within expressions that are invalid (for the correctness-related typing rules) or malleable (for the malleability-related typing rules) anyway, but it does mean that exact type tests like the ones in `malleable_from_alloy.txt` enforce than strictly needed.

In fact, rust-miniscript, Bitcoin Core, and the BIP text are all inconsistent with each other, in minor irrelevant ways. If we want to go the direction of having strict test vectors (which I support), I think we also need to first align all implementations and specifications. My suggestion would be to make everything match the BIP text. I have an (LLM written) patch for Bitcoin Core to make it do that (which passes all its unit & fuzz tests) which I'm happy to PR, but someone else will need to do the same for rust-bitcoin. It differs from the BIP in one rule: the `thresh` rule for the "unique dissatisfiable" `e` rule in the BIP is that all children are `s`, while rust-miniscript (and Bitcoin Core, so far) additionally (and superfluously) require that all children are `e`.

> My suggestion would be to make everything match the BIP text.

(non-author) approach ACK

Thanks a lot for testing the test vectors with Bitcoin Core, @sipa.

I'm also in favor of attempting to align everything with the BIP text.

> but someone else will need to do the same for rust-bitcoin

Will attempt that soon-ish.

EDIT: Here's the [BIP amendment PR](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/2267) and the [`rust-miniscript` PR](https://github.com/rust-bitcoin/rust-miniscript/pull/1032).
I I've pushed up a fixup commit (3526e43) that addresses https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/2240#issuecomment-5347499382 (and also fixes the Golang import issues I didn't realize were there).

concept ACK. Great effort. I'm sure a LLM can fill in the documented gaps in a followup PR.

I didn't look at the test vectors or the Go code, but the markdown updates look good to me.

Will review https://github.com/rust-bitcoin/rust-miniscript/pull/1032 more carefully.

I've updated the test vectors in a fixup commit to match the discussion in https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/2267 and the proposed changes in https://github.com/rust-bitcoin/rust-miniscript/pull/1037.

events.body: Thanks for the reviews and updates to the implementations, great to see that y’all are on it.

The harness compares sat_witness_elements and sat_size, and both count as rust-miniscript does. The BIP does not say what they count. An implementation that counts as Bitcoin Core does fails every sat_witness_elements row and 21% of sat_size rows.

I ran the vectors at 47047eb through btclib-wallet's miniscript module, which reproduces the resource numbers in Core's miniscript_tests.cpp. Once malleable expressions carry no "s", "f" or "e", as #2267 says, it agrees on every row for validity, types, timelock mixing, malleability, requires_sig, script_size and both script tables. It also disagrees on 10% of the opcodes.txt ops and on op_count and exec_stack, none of which the harness compares.

Two examples. `pk(A)` has sat_witness_elements 2 where Core counts 1: the vector counts the witness script, which the BIP's 100-element rule excludes. In the Tapscript table, `thresh(1,pk(A),s:pk(B))` has sat_size 132, two 66-byte signatures, and no valid witness is that large. Two valid signatures make the count 2, not 1. Under BIP342 a failed non-empty signature fails the script, so the key that does not sign gives an empty signature. The largest witness is then 67, which is what Core gives. Other differences come from dissatisfactions Core does not count, such as a hash's.

Could the Files table say what each of these columns counts, or could the harness skip sat_witness_elements and sat_size as it does op_count and exec_stack?

Thanks for running the vectors against `btclib`, that's very useful independent validation.

There were two separate issues:

- **`thresh` was a bug.** The extraction sized k+1 satisfied sub expressions instead of k (fixed upstream in rust-bitcoin/rust-miniscript#1040). The regenerated tables now give 67 for `thresh(1,pk(A),s:pk(B))`, the same as you got.
- **The rest is how the columns are counted.** They follow `rust-miniscript`: `sat_witness_elements` adds one for the witness script, and `op_count` / `sat_size` maximize over all satisfactions, malleable ones included. Core never dissatisfies a hash fragment. Changing only that rule in the Go implementation reproduces your figures: 9.6% of `opcodes.txt` ops and 20–22% of `sat_size` rows.

I went with your first suggestion and updated the PR:

- A new "Resource Columns" section defines each column and states the difference from Core. `exec_stack` and the Tapscript `op_count` are marked informative only.
- New `limits[_tap].txt` has within/over vectors at each limit (201 ops, 3,600 bytes, 100 witness elements, 1,000 Tapscript stack elements), with no hash fragments. Core and the Go implementation agree on all ten verdicts. `rust-miniscript` rejects the 100-element `within` vector, because it counts the witness script against that limit.
- The harness now compares types, op counts and the limit verdicts. It skips only `exec_stack` and the Tapscript `op_count`.
- Everything now comes from unmodified `rust-miniscript` master (`698b97f`).

ACK 217afc1416d1d51f97ac3c3b1c70a306ce7ce242

I ran the vectors through btclib-wallet's miniscript module (not redeem.json, and not the Go harness). Parsing, types, scripts and the ten limit verdicts agree. The resource columns differ only by the two rules the new section describes, apart from `exec_stack` and the Tapscript `op_count`, which the section already sets aside.

Two wording nits. The Files table says every line of `conflict_from_alloy.txt` mixes timelock kinds on one path, but 187 of the 1,773 do not, for example `and_v(v:multi(2,A,B,C),andor(multi(2,D,E,F),after(500000001),after(1)))`, which `props_from_rust.tsv` marks `mixed_timelocks=false`. And `edge_cases.txt` is not "the only hand-written file": `limits.txt` and `limits_tap.txt` are too.
